name: ERP & SAP FI/CO
title: FI/CO Specialist
blurb: SAP FI/CO is one of Arin's three target roles, and Japanese SAP consultancies hire graduates who can already explain how a business transaction flows through S/4HANA finance and controlling.

chapters.title: ERP concepts and end-to-end processes
chapters.read: SAP Learning (learning.sap.com) introductory journeys on S/4HANA business processes: what ERP integration means, and the steps of record-to-report (R2R), procure-to-pay (P2P, FI-MM) and order-to-cash (O2C, FI-SD), including which steps create accounting entries.
chapters.produce: Draw three swimlane diagrams (R2R, P2P, O2C) for a small Kofu wine distributor, marking every step that posts to the G/L with its debit and credit.

quiz.q: What is the main benefit of an integrated ERP system such as SAP S/4HANA?
opts: Each department keeps its own database, reconciled with the others at month-end
A transaction entered once updates every affected area, e.g. a goods receipt updates stock and the G/L at the same time
It removes the need for a chart of accounts
It removes the need for approval workflows and internal controls
quiz.ex: Integration means one shared database: logistics and finance see the same transaction immediately, so there is no re-keying or month-end reconciliation between modules.

quiz.q: Which is the correct order of the procure-to-pay (P2P) process?
opts: Purchase order, purchase requisition, invoice receipt, goods receipt, payment
Purchase requisition, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice receipt, payment
Invoice receipt, purchase order, goods receipt, payment, purchase requisition
Purchase requisition, payment, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice receipt
quiz.ex: A need is raised (requisition), turned into an order to the supplier, the goods arrive, the supplier's invoice is checked against PO and GR, and then it is paid.

quiz.q: Which is the correct order of the order-to-cash (O2C) process?
opts: Billing, sales order, incoming payment, outbound delivery
Outbound delivery, billing, sales order, incoming payment
Sales order, incoming payment, billing, outbound delivery
Sales order, outbound delivery with goods issue, billing, incoming payment
quiz.ex: The customer orders, goods are picked and issued, an invoice (billing document) is created, and finally the customer pays.

quiz.q: In P2P, a goods receipt for stock material valued at its purchase price normally posts which entry?
opts: Dr Inventory, Cr GR/IR clearing account
Dr GR/IR clearing account, Cr Vendor
Dr Inventory, Cr Vendor
Dr Expense, Cr Bank
quiz.ex: At GR the supplier has not invoiced yet, so the credit goes to the GR/IR clearing account; the vendor is credited later at invoice receipt, which clears GR/IR.

quiz.q: In O2C, what does the goods issue for a delivery post in FI?
opts: Dr Customer, Cr Revenue
Dr Cost of goods sold, Cr Inventory
Dr Inventory, Cr Cost of goods sold
Dr Bank, Cr Customer
quiz.ex: Goods issue removes stock and expenses its cost. Revenue and the receivable are posted later, by billing.

quiz.q: What does record-to-report (R2R) cover?
opts: Raising purchase requisitions through to receiving goods
Receiving IT support requests through to resolving them
Recording journal entries, closing the books and producing financial statements
Recruiting employees through to their retirement
quiz.ex: R2R is the finance core process: capture transactions in the G/L, run period-end closing, and report.

chapters.title: FI enterprise structure
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on FI organisational units and global settings: company code, chart of accounts types (operational, group, country), fiscal year variants and special periods, posting period variants, document types and number ranges.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page enterprise-structure design for a fictional Japanese group with two company codes (Japan, Singapore): which chart of accounts, fiscal year variant, posting period variant and document types each uses, with a one-line reason for each choice.

quiz.q: Which definition describes an SAP company code?
opts: A grouping of plants used for material requirements planning
The top-level unit used only for internal cost accounting
A unit that groups sales organisations for pricing
The smallest organisational unit for which a complete, self-contained set of accounts can be drawn up for external reporting
quiz.ex: Legal-entity balance sheets and P&Ls are produced at company-code level; internal cost accounting happens in the controlling area.

quiz.q: A fiscal year variant has 12 regular posting periods plus the maximum number of special periods allowed. How many periods in total can be posted to in that fiscal year?
quiz.ex: 12 regular periods + 4 special periods = 16. Special periods are used for year-end adjustments such as audit entries.

quiz.q: What does a posting period variant do?
opts: Defines how many periods the fiscal year has
Controls which posting periods are open for posting, and can be assigned to several company codes so they are opened and closed together
Defines the exchange rate type used for each period
Assigns a chart of accounts to each period
quiz.ex: The fiscal year variant defines the periods; the posting period variant opens and closes them. Sharing one variant across company codes lets you close them in one step.

quiz.q: How are operational charts of accounts and company codes related?
opts: Each company code must have its own unique operational chart of accounts
A chart of accounts is assigned to a plant, not a company code
Each company code uses exactly one operational chart of accounts, and several company codes may share the same one
A company code can post to several operational charts of accounts at the same time
quiz.ex: Sharing one operational chart of accounts makes group reporting simpler; local legal needs can be met with a country chart of accounts as an alternative.

quiz.q: What is a document type mainly used for in SAP FI?
opts: To store the exchange rates used in the document
To classify postings and control which account types may be posted and which number range the document numbers come from
To define the customer's payment terms
To calculate the consumption tax amount
quiz.ex: Document types (e.g. vendor invoice, customer invoice, G/L document) carry the number range and the allowed account types.

quiz.q: In a standard SAP system, which document type is used for a vendor invoice posted directly in FI?
opts: DR
KR
SA
DZ
quiz.ex: KR is the vendor invoice; DR is the customer invoice, SA a general G/L document, and DZ a customer payment.

chapters.title: General Ledger
chapters.read: SAP Learning journey on General Ledger accounting in S/4HANA: G/L account master data (chart-of-accounts and company-code segments), account types, open item management, reconciliation accounts, posting keys, ledgers, document splitting and the financial statement version.
chapters.produce: Design 25 G/L accounts for a small trading company (account number, name, type, open-item managed or not, reconciliation account type) and explain in writing where each would appear in the financial statement version.

quiz.q: How is a G/L account master record split in SAP?
opts: A chart-of-accounts segment (e.g. number, name, account type) and a company-code segment (e.g. account currency, open item management, tax category)
A sales-area segment and a purchasing-organisation segment
A plant segment and a storage-location segment
A controlling-area segment only; company codes do not store G/L settings
quiz.ex: Settings shared by everyone using the chart of accounts sit in the chart-of-accounts segment; settings that can differ per company code sit in the company-code segment.

quiz.q: Which kind of G/L account is typically managed on an open-item basis?
opts: Revenue accounts
Retained earnings
Depreciation expense
Clearing accounts such as the GR/IR clearing account or a bank clearing account
quiz.ex: Open item management is for accounts whose entries must be offset (cleared) against each other, so you can see what is still outstanding.

quiz.q: Which statement about reconciliation accounts is correct?
opts: They must be posted to manually at month-end to match the subledgers
They are used only in Controlling, not in FI
They are profit and loss accounts
They are updated automatically by subledger postings (customer, vendor, asset) and cannot be posted to directly
quiz.ex: Every customer, vendor or asset posting also hits its reconciliation account in real time, so subledger and G/L always agree.

quiz.q: In standard SAP, what do posting keys 40 and 50 mean?
opts: 40 = credit a vendor, 50 = debit a vendor
40 = debit a customer, 50 = credit a customer
40 = debit a G/L account, 50 = credit a G/L account
40 = debit an asset, 50 = credit an asset
quiz.ex: The posting key sets the account type and the debit/credit side; 40/50 are the standard G/L debit/credit keys.

quiz.q: What is document splitting used for?
opts: To split a large document into several smaller documents for performance
To divide a vendor invoice between several vendors
To spread an expense across several fiscal years
To produce balanced balance sheets and P&Ls for characteristics such as profit centre or segment
quiz.ex: Splitting assigns balance-sheet lines such as payables and tax to profit centres or segments, so a full balance sheet can be drawn up for each.

quiz.q: At year-end, the P&L accounts of a company code show revenue ¥9,000,000 (credit) and expenses ¥6,500,000 (debit). How much does the balance carryforward move into the retained earnings account (enter the profit as a positive number)?
quiz.ex: P&L accounts are carried forward to retained earnings: 9,000,000 − 6,500,000 = 2,500,000 profit.

chapters.title: Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable
chapters.read: SAP Learning journeys on AP and AR in S/4HANA: supplier and customer master data as business partner roles, invoices and credit memos, payment terms and cash discounts, the automatic payment program, dunning, partial and residual payments, and special G/L transactions such as down payments.
chapters.produce: Walk one supplier invoice and one customer invoice through their full life on paper (invoice, payment proposal or dunning, payment, clearing), writing the journal entry at each step with consumption tax.

quiz.q: Which sequence matches the automatic payment program?
opts: Enter parameters, run the proposal, review and edit the proposal, execute the payment run, create the payment medium
Execute the payment run, enter parameters, run the proposal, create the payment medium
Create the payment medium, run the proposal, enter parameters, execute the payment run
Run the proposal, create the payment medium, enter parameters, execute the payment run
quiz.ex: Parameters (date, company codes, payment methods, suppliers) come first; the proposal can be checked and edited before the actual run posts payments and creates bank files.

quiz.q: What does the dunning program do?
opts: Pays overdue supplier invoices automatically
Selects overdue customer open items and sends reminder letters according to dunning levels
Writes off all overdue receivables to expense
Revalues foreign-currency receivables at period-end
quiz.ex: Dunning is the AR collections tool: the higher the dunning level, the stronger the reminder.

quiz.q: A supplier invoice is ¥200,000 net plus 10% consumption tax. What amount is credited to the supplier account?
quiz.ex: 200,000 + 10% × 200,000 = 220,000. The expense or GR/IR gets 200,000 and input tax 20,000.

quiz.q: A customer invoice of ¥500,000 has payment terms '2% discount within 10 days, net 30'. The customer pays on day 7 and takes the discount. How much cash is received?
quiz.ex: Paid inside the discount period: 500,000 × (1 − 0.02) = 490,000; 10,000 is posted as cash discount.

quiz.q: How are special G/L transactions such as supplier down payments kept separate from normal payables?
opts: They post to a separate company code
They are recorded only in Controlling
They are not posted until the final invoice arrives
They post to an alternative reconciliation account selected by a special G/L indicator
quiz.ex: The special G/L indicator swaps in a different reconciliation account, so down payments show separately on the balance sheet.

quiz.q: A customer pays only part of an invoice. What is the difference between a partial payment and a residual payment?
opts: A partial payment clears the invoice; a residual payment leaves it open
Both clear the invoice and write off the remainder
A residual payment is only possible for suppliers, never for customers
A partial payment leaves the original invoice open with the payment as a linked open item; a residual payment clears the invoice and creates a new open item for the rest
quiz.ex: With a partial payment both items stay open until fully paid; with a residual payment the original is cleared and only the remaining amount stays open.

chapters.title: Asset Accounting (new Asset Accounting in S/4)
chapters.read: SAP Learning journey on Asset Accounting in S/4HANA: asset classes, depreciation areas and keys, acquisition, assets under construction, retirement, the depreciation run, and how new Asset Accounting posts parallel valuations in real time to the Universal Journal.
chapters.produce: Build a spreadsheet asset register for 5 assets showing monthly straight-line depreciation and one retirement with gain or loss, and write the matching SAP postings.

quiz.q: What is an asset class used for?
opts: It groups similar assets and supplies defaults such as account determination and depreciation terms to each asset master
It defines the company code's fiscal year
It stores the asset's acquisition cost
It decides which bank pays the asset supplier
quiz.ex: Asset classes (e.g. buildings, vehicles, IT equipment) control which G/L accounts are hit and give default depreciation settings.

quiz.q: Why does an asset have several depreciation areas?
opts: To spread the asset over several company codes
To record the asset in several currencies only
To store the asset's maintenance history
To value the same asset in parallel, e.g. for different accounting principles such as local GAAP and IFRS, or for tax
quiz.ex: Each depreciation area can have its own useful life, method and values.

quiz.q: A machine costs ¥1,200,000, has no residual value and a 5-year useful life with straight-line depreciation, starting at the beginning of the fiscal year. What is its net book value after 2 full years?
What is an asset under construction (AuC)?
opts: An asset that collects costs while it is being built, then is settled to one or more final assets when complete
An asset that is already fully depreciated
A leased asset that the company does not own
An asset that is held for sale
quiz.ex: AuCs are usually not depreciated; once the building or machine is ready, its costs are settled to the final asset, which then starts depreciating.

quiz.q: Which statement fits new Asset Accounting in S/4HANA?
opts: Parallel valuations post in real time to their ledgers, and asset postings are stored in the Universal Journal
Only one depreciation area can be used per asset
Asset values are kept in separate tables that are reconciled with the G/L at year-end
Depreciation can only be posted once per fiscal year
quiz.ex: New Asset Accounting is integrated with the ledgers: each valuation is posted when it happens and the line items are in ACDOCA.

quiz.q: An asset with acquisition cost ¥500,000 and accumulated depreciation ¥350,000 is sold for ¥200,000. What is the gain on disposal?

chapters.title: Bank Accounting
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on Bank Accounting in S/4HANA: house banks and house bank accounts, bank account management, the electronic bank statement and its posting rules, bank clearing (interim) accounts, the cash journal, and bank reconciliation.
chapters.produce: Prepare a bank reconciliation for a month with 10 bank statement lines and 3 timing differences, and map each statement line to the posting rule (debit, credit, clearing) it would trigger.

quiz.q: What is a house bank in SAP?
opts: Any bank used by a customer to pay the company
The central bank of the company code's country
A bank where the company code holds its own accounts, each set up as a house bank account linked to a G/L account
A cash box used for petty cash
quiz.ex: House banks and their accounts are used by the payment program and the bank statement to find the right G/L accounts.

quiz.q: What does the electronic bank statement do?
opts: Sends payment orders to the bank
Calculates the company's credit rating
Revalues foreign-currency bank balances
Imports statement lines and uses posting rules to post them and clear matching open items automatically
quiz.ex: Statement lines are interpreted (e.g. by matching the reference to an invoice or payment) and then posted to the bank and clearing accounts.

quiz.q: Why are bank clearing (interim) accounts used for outgoing payments?
opts: They store the bank's interest rates
They hold the payment until the bank statement confirms the money has actually left the main bank account
They replace the vendor reconciliation account
They are needed only for cash payments
quiz.ex: The payment run credits the clearing account; when the statement arrives, the clearing account is cleared against the main bank account, which then matches the bank.

quiz.q: At month-end the company's book balance for a bank account is ¥1,000,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented total ¥150,000, and a deposit of ¥80,000 is in transit (recorded in the books, not yet on the statement). What balance should the bank statement show?
quiz.ex: Bank = book + outstanding cheques − deposits in transit = 1,000,000 + 150,000 − 80,000 = 1,070,000.

quiz.q: Which pair are common electronic bank statement formats?
opts: MT103 and pain.001
ORDERS and DESADV IDocs
MT940 and camt.053
PDF and JPEG
quiz.ex: MT940 (SWIFT) and camt.053 (ISO 20022) are statement formats. MT103 and pain.001 are payment instructions, not statements.

quiz.q: What is the cash journal for?
opts: Recording small cash receipts and payments (petty cash) with a running balance per cash box
Importing bank statements
Running the automatic payment program
Recording foreign exchange deals
quiz.ex: The cash journal is a simple tool for petty cash, posting to a cash G/L account.

chapters.title: Period-end closing
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on financial close in S/4HANA: accruals and deferrals, foreign currency valuation, GR/IR regrouping, depreciation run, cost allocations and settlements, opening and closing periods, and balance carryforward.
chapters.produce: Write a month-end closing checklist of 15 steps for a company using FI and CO, with the order, the owner (AP, AR, GL, CO) and the check that proves each step is done.

quiz.q: What does foreign currency valuation do at period-end?
opts: Revalues foreign-currency open items and balances at the period-end rate, posting unrealised exchange gains or losses
Converts all transactions into USD for group reporting
Changes the company code currency
Clears all foreign-currency invoices
quiz.ex: Open payables, receivables and FX bank balances are restated at the closing rate.

quiz.q: A supplier invoice of USD 10,000 was posted at ¥145/USD and is still unpaid at month-end, when the rate is ¥150/USD. What unrealised exchange loss is posted?
quiz.ex: Liability rises from 1,450,000 to 1,500,000, so the loss is 10,000 × (150 − 145) = 50,000.

quiz.q: Why are posting periods closed after month-end?
opts: To stop postings into a period whose figures have already been reported
To delete documents from that period
To recalculate depreciation automatically
To archive the chart of accounts
quiz.ex: Closing periods protects reported numbers; any later adjustment must go into an open period or a special period.

quiz.q: What does balance carryforward do at fiscal year change?
opts: Deletes all P&L documents of the old year
Carries P&L account balances forward unchanged
Pays all open supplier items
Carries balance sheet balances into the new year and moves the P&L result to the retained earnings account
quiz.ex: Balance sheet accounts keep their balances; P&L accounts start the new year at zero, with the result in retained earnings.

quiz.q: What is GR/IR regrouping for?
opts: Reclassifying GR/IR balances into 'goods received, not invoiced' and 'invoiced, not received' for correct balance sheet presentation
Clearing all GR/IR items against expense
Paying suppliers for goods received
Revaluing inventory at standard price
quiz.ex: A debit balance (invoice before goods) and a credit balance (goods before invoice) are different things, so they are shown separately.

quiz.q: A December electricity bill will only arrive in January. What is the usual month-end entry in December?
opts: No entry until the bill arrives
Dr Accrued liabilities, Cr Utilities expense
Dr Utilities expense, Cr Accrued liabilities, reversed at the start of January
Dr Prepaid expenses, Cr Bank
quiz.ex: Accruals put the expense into the period it belongs to; reversing it in January avoids double-counting when the real invoice is posted.

chapters.title: CO: cost elements, cost centres and internal orders
chapters.read: SAP Learning journey on Overhead Cost Controlling in S/4HANA: the controlling area, cost elements as G/L accounts (primary and secondary), cost centres and the standard hierarchy, activity types, assessments and distributions, and internal orders with settlement rules and budgets.
chapters.produce: Set up on paper a cost centre hierarchy for a 50-person company, then allocate one month of IT and building costs to the other cost centres by headcount and floor space, and run one marketing internal order through to settlement.

quiz.q: How are cost elements handled in S/4HANA?
opts: They are a separate CO master record with no link to G/L accounts
Only balance sheet accounts can be cost elements
Cost elements no longer exist and costs are posted only to profit centres
They are G/L accounts; P&L accounts are primary cost elements, and secondary cost elements are G/L accounts used only for internal allocations
quiz.ex: In S/4 the cost element is an attribute of the G/L account (with a cost element category), so FI and CO share one master record.

quiz.q: What are secondary cost elements used for?
opts: Internal CO allocations such as assessments, activity allocations and settlements
Posting supplier invoices
Recording bank fees
Posting depreciation in Asset Accounting
quiz.ex: Secondary costs move costs between CO objects; they cancel out across the company and have no external P&L effect.

quiz.q: What is the difference between a distribution and an assessment?
opts: Distribution is for internal orders only; assessment is for assets only
Distribution keeps the original primary cost element on the receiver; assessment uses a secondary (assessment) cost element
Assessment keeps the original primary cost element; distribution uses a secondary cost element
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
quiz.ex: Use distribution when receivers must see the original cost type (e.g. rent); use assessment when one combined amount is enough.

quiz.q: The IT cost centre has ¥900,000 of costs, allocated by headcount: Sales 30, Production 50, Admin 20. How much does Production receive?
What is a statistical internal order?
opts: An order that records costs for information only; the real cost assignment must go to another object such as a cost centre
An order that can be settled to several receivers
An order used only for revenue
An order that has a budget but never receives costs
quiz.ex: Statistical orders are for extra reporting; they cannot be settled because the real costs sit elsewhere.

quiz.q: What does an internal order's settlement rule define?
opts: The order's approval workflow
The exchange rate used for the order
The receivers (e.g. cost centre, asset, G/L account) and the shares to which the order's costs are passed
The posting period in which the order was created
quiz.ex: At period-end, settlement credits the order and debits the receivers according to the rule.

chapters.title: CO: profit centres, product costing and CO-PA
chapters.read: SAP Learning journeys on Profit Center Accounting, Product Cost Planning and Margin Analysis in S/4HANA: profit centres in the General Ledger, standard cost estimates (BOM, routing, activity prices, overhead), price control S and V, variances, and account-based profitability analysis.
chapters.produce: Calculate a standard cost estimate for one product (materials, two activities, overhead), then compute the price and production variances for one month and show where they land in margin analysis.

quiz.q: Where does profit centre accounting live in S/4HANA?
opts: In a separate ledger that is reconciled with FI at month-end
In the General Ledger: the profit centre is a field on each Universal Journal line
Only in Asset Accounting
Only in sales orders, not in accounting
quiz.ex: Classic separate profit centre ledgers are replaced by the profit centre field in ACDOCA, often combined with document splitting.

quiz.q: What is the difference between price control S and V on a material?
opts: S is for services and V is for valuables
S values stock at a fixed standard price and sends differences to price-difference accounts; V values stock at a moving average price
S updates the price with every goods receipt; V never changes
S is used only for finished goods and V only for raw materials, by system rule
quiz.ex: With S the inventory value is predictable and variances are shown separately; with V each receipt changes the average price.

quiz.q: A material uses price control S with a standard price of ¥100 per unit. 1,000 units are received against a purchase order at ¥105 per unit. What amount is posted to the price difference account?
quiz.ex: Inventory is debited at standard: 1,000 × 100 = 100,000. GR/IR is credited at PO price: 105,000. The 5,000 difference goes to price differences.

quiz.q: What is the quantity structure of a standard cost estimate for a manufactured product?
opts: Purchase orders and invoices
Sales orders and deliveries
Bill of materials (BOM) and routing
Cost centre hierarchy and profit centre hierarchy
quiz.ex: The BOM gives the components and quantities; the routing gives the operations and the activity quantities to be valued.

quiz.q: Which statement about account-based CO-PA (margin analysis) is correct?
opts: It uses value fields that are not linked to G/L accounts
It cannot report by customer or product
It uses G/L accounts, so it always reconciles with FI, and it is SAP's recommended approach in S/4HANA
It is updated only once a year
quiz.ex: Margin analysis characteristics (customer, product, region…) are stored on the Universal Journal lines, so profitability and the P&L come from the same data.

quiz.q: A product's standard cost estimate has materials ¥4,000, 2 machine hours at ¥1,500 per hour, and overhead of 10% on materials. What is the standard cost per unit?
quiz.ex: Materials 4,000 + activities 2 × 1,500 = 3,000 + overhead 10% × 4,000 = 400. Total 7,400.

chapters.title: S/4HANA specifics: Universal Journal, Business Partner, Fiori
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on what changed from ECC to S/4HANA in finance: the SAP HANA in-memory column database, the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), compatibility views, the mandatory Business Partner with customer/vendor integration (CVI), and the Fiori launchpad and role-based apps.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page 'ECC vs S/4HANA Finance' comparison for a client CFO covering data model, master data and user experience, with one concrete benefit for month-end closing.

quiz.q: What is the Universal Journal (ACDOCA)?
opts: A table holding only sales orders
A single line-item table holding FI, CO, Asset Accounting and Material Ledger data together
A separate database for audit logs
A reporting cube refreshed overnight
quiz.ex: One line in ACDOCA carries G/L account, cost centre, profit centre, segment, asset and more, so there is one source of truth.

quiz.q: What is a direct benefit of FI and CO sharing the Universal Journal?
opts: There is no FI-CO reconciliation step, because both read the same line items
CO no longer needs cost centres
Posting periods no longer need closing
All postings are made in USD
quiz.ex: In ECC, FI and CO stored data separately and needed reconciliation; in S/4 they are the same records.

quiz.q: What is the role of the Business Partner in S/4HANA?
opts: It is an optional add-on used only for CRM
It replaces the chart of accounts
It is the mandatory central master data object; customers and suppliers are created as business partners with roles
It is used only for employees
quiz.ex: Customer/vendor integration (CVI) keeps the customer and supplier records in sync with the business partner.

quiz.q: What is SAP Fiori?
opts: A database that replaces SAP HANA
SAP's role-based user experience, with apps started from the Fiori launchpad in a web browser
A programming language for SAP reports
A tool for migrating data into S/4HANA
quiz.ex: Fiori apps are grouped by business role and can show live analytics because they read HANA directly.

quiz.q: What happened to many classic FI totals and index tables in S/4HANA?
opts: They were moved to a separate archive server
They were replaced by compatibility views calculated from the Universal Journal, so the data is not stored twice
They are still updated in parallel for every posting
They became the main table instead of ACDOCA
quiz.ex: HANA can aggregate line items on the fly, so redundant totals and indexes are no longer needed; old programs still read them as views.

quiz.q: Why can S/4HANA aggregate large volumes of line items quickly?
opts: It stores only monthly totals
It deletes old line items every month
It runs all reports overnight in batch
SAP HANA is an in-memory, column-oriented database
quiz.ex: Columnar, in-memory storage makes scanning and summing a single column very fast.

chapters.title: Migration, SAP Activate and testing
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on S/4HANA transition paths (new implementation, system conversion, selective data transition), the SAP Activate methodology and its phases, fit-to-standard workshops, data migration of master data and open items, and test types from unit to user acceptance testing.
chapters.produce: Write a 2-page migration recommendation for a fictional ECC client choosing between greenfield, brownfield and selective transition, plus a test plan listing test types, owners and exit criteria for go-live.

quiz.q: What is a greenfield transition to S/4HANA?
opts: A new implementation with redesigned processes, loading master data, open items and balances from the old system
A technical conversion of the existing ECC system that keeps all configuration and history
Moving only selected company codes with full history
Upgrading the database without changing the application
quiz.ex: Greenfield starts clean: good for simplifying, but full transaction history is not carried across.

quiz.q: What is a brownfield transition?
opts: A brand-new implementation on a fresh system
Running ECC and S/4 in parallel forever
A system conversion of an existing ECC system to S/4HANA, keeping configuration, custom code and history
Moving to a non-SAP ERP
quiz.ex: Brownfield protects past investment and history but also carries over old design choices.

quiz.q: When does selective data transition fit best?
opts: When the client wants an exact copy of ECC
When the client has no historic data at all
When the client wants a new design but needs to bring selected data, such as certain company codes or years of history
When only the user interface should change
quiz.ex: It sits between greenfield and brownfield, and is usually done with specialist tools and partners.

quiz.q: What is the order of the SAP Activate phases?
opts: Prepare, Discover, Realize, Explore, Run, Deploy
Explore, Prepare, Discover, Deploy, Realize, Run
Discover, Prepare, Explore, Realize, Deploy, Run
Discover, Explore, Prepare, Realize, Run, Deploy
quiz.ex: Activate starts with discovering value, prepares the project, explores the standard, builds (realizes), deploys to production and then runs.

quiz.q: In which SAP Activate phase are fit-to-standard workshops held?
opts: Discover
Deploy
Run
Explore
quiz.ex: In Explore, consultants show standard processes and record gaps (the delta requirements) to be built in Realize.

quiz.q: Which test checks that functions that worked before still work after a change or upgrade?
opts: Regression testing
Unit testing
Performance testing
Exploratory testing
quiz.ex: Regression tests re-run existing scenarios to catch side effects of changes.

chapters.title: Japan setup: consumption tax, invoices and parallel ledgers
chapters.read: Japanese tax authority (国税庁) English pages on consumption tax (消費税) and the qualified invoice system (インボイス制度), plus SAP Learning material on tax codes and parallel accounting with leading and non-leading ledgers; learn the concepts only, not detailed configuration.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page note for a Japanese subsidiary explaining which tax codes it needs (10%, 8%, exempt, non-taxable), what a qualified invoice must show, and how J-GAAP and IFRS would be kept in parallel ledgers.

quiz.q: What are Japan's consumption tax rates?
opts: 8% standard and 5% reduced for all food
10% on everything, with no reduced rate
10% standard and 8% reduced, the reduced rate covering food and drink (excluding alcohol and eating out) and certain newspaper subscriptions
15% standard and 10% reduced
quiz.ex: Since October 2019 Japan has had a 10% standard rate and an 8% reduced rate.

quiz.q: A supplier's invoice lists food items of ¥3,000 (8% rate) and household goods of ¥5,000 (10% rate), both before tax. What is the total consumption tax?
What does a registration number on a qualified invoice (適格請求書) look like?
opts: The letter J followed by 10 digits
The company's phone number
The letter T followed by 13 digits
An 8-digit number with no letter
quiz.ex: Registered issuers get a number of 'T' plus 13 digits, which must appear on the qualified invoice.

quiz.q: Under the qualified invoice system, how is consumption tax rounding done on one invoice?
opts: Separately on each line item, then added up
Always rounded up to the nearest ¥10
No rounding is allowed; tax is shown in decimals
Once per tax rate per invoice, not separately on each line item
quiz.ex: The tax is calculated on the total for each rate and rounded once per rate, which tax code and invoice design in SAP must respect.

quiz.q: How is parallel accounting for IFRS and J-GAAP typically set up using the ledger approach in S/4HANA?
opts: Two separate company codes for the same legal entity
Separate G/L accounts for every IFRS and J-GAAP value in one ledger
One ledger, with differences kept in a spreadsheet
A leading ledger (0L) for one standard, e.g. IFRS, and a non-leading ledger for the other, with ledger-specific postings only where values differ
quiz.ex: Common postings go to all ledgers; differences such as depreciation or goodwill are posted only to the ledger concerned.

quiz.q: Which is a well-known difference between J-GAAP and IFRS?
opts: Goodwill is amortised under J-GAAP but not under IFRS, where it is tested for impairment instead
Only IFRS requires a balance sheet
J-GAAP does not allow depreciation
IFRS requires the fiscal year to end in March
quiz.ex: Under J-GAAP goodwill is amortised over a period of up to 20 years; IFRS bans amortisation and requires an annual impairment test.

boss.q: A goods receipt for ¥100,000 was posted earlier. The supplier's invoice now arrives for ¥100,000 net plus 10% consumption tax, matching the PO. Which entry does invoice verification post?
opts: Dr Inventory 110,000; Cr Supplier 110,000
Dr GR/IR 100,000; Dr Input tax 10,000; Cr Supplier 110,000
Dr GR/IR 110,000; Cr Supplier 100,000; Cr Input tax 10,000
Dr Supplier 110,000; Cr GR/IR 100,000; Cr Input tax 10,000
boss.ex: Invoice receipt clears the GR/IR credit from the goods receipt, records claimable input tax, and creates the payable for the gross amount.

boss.q: What is the difference between the accounts approach and the ledger approach to parallel accounting?
opts: The accounts approach needs separate company codes; the ledger approach does not
The ledger approach is only for Controlling; the accounts approach is only for FI
The accounts approach uses separate G/L accounts for valuation differences within one ledger; the ledger approach keeps each accounting standard in its own ledger
They are the same thing with different names
boss.ex: Both solve parallel reporting; the ledger approach keeps the account structure the same for every standard.

boss.q: An asset costing ¥2,400,000 has a 4-year useful life, straight-line, no residual value, and monthly pro-rata depreciation starting in the month of acquisition. It is acquired at the start of period 4 of a 12-period fiscal year. What is the depreciation for that first fiscal year?
boss.ex: Monthly depreciation = 2,400,000 / 48 = 50,000. Periods 4 to 12 = 9 months, so 9 × 50,000 = 450,000.

boss.q: A customer invoice of USD 20,000 was posted at ¥150/USD. The customer pays the full USD 20,000 when the rate is ¥147/USD. What realised exchange loss is posted?
The maintenance cost centre provides 120 hours to the production cost centre at an activity price of ¥4,000 per hour. By how much is the maintenance cost centre credited?
boss.ex: Activity allocation credits the sender with quantity × price: 120 × 4,000 = 480,000, using a secondary cost element.

boss.q: In a brownfield conversion from ECC, what must be done for customer and supplier master data before the technical conversion?
opts: Convert them to business partners through customer/vendor integration (CVI)
Delete them and recreate them manually after go-live
Nothing; S/4HANA keeps using customer and vendor masters without business partners
Move them into Controlling as cost centres
boss.ex: Business partner is mandatory in S/4HANA, so CVI synchronisation is a prerequisite step for the conversion.

boss.q: A user tries to post a manual G/L journal directly to the accounts payable reconciliation account. What happens?
opts: The posting succeeds and creates a new supplier
The system rejects it, because reconciliation accounts can only be posted through the supplier subledger
The posting succeeds but only in Controlling
The posting is split automatically across all suppliers
boss.ex: Blocking direct postings is what keeps the subledger and the G/L in agreement.

boss.q: Goodwill of ¥10,000,000 is amortised straight-line over 10 years under J-GAAP and not amortised under IFRS. With IFRS in the leading ledger and J-GAAP in a non-leading ledger, what annual amortisation is posted to the J-GAAP ledger only?
boss.ex: 10,000,000 / 10 = 1,000,000 per year, posted only to the J-GAAP ledger; the IFRS ledger gets no amortisation (impairment testing instead).

boss.q: A client wants to redesign its finance processes on S/4HANA but must keep 5 years of history for two of its six company codes. Which transition path fits best?
opts: Greenfield with only open items migrated
Brownfield system conversion of all six company codes
Stay on ECC and add Fiori apps
Selective data transition
boss.ex: Selective transition allows a new design while bringing chosen data, here specific company codes and years.

boss.q: A product uses price control S. At period-end, a production order shows actual costs above its target costs. Where does the difference end up after settlement?
opts: Added to the material's standard price automatically
Credited from the order and posted as a production variance, which can also be reported in margin analysis
Left on the production order forever
Posted to the supplier's account
boss.ex: Under standard costing the stock stays at standard; order settlement moves the variance to the P&L and margin analysis.
